claim: Psilocybin-assisted therapy produces durable remission in treatment-resistant depression
gold_rationale: As of mid-2026 the evidence base has moved from "insufficient" toward genuinely contested, but durable REMISSION in TRD is still not established as clinical/regulatory consensus. The pivotal phase 2b P-TRD trial (Goodwin/COMPASS, NEJM 2022, NCT03775200, N=233) hit its Week-3 MADRS primary endpoint for 25 mg but explicitly reported that sustained response at 12 weeks was NOT supportive of the primary result (DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa2206443) — the surrogate short-term signal did not translate to durability. The head-to-head phase 2 trial vs escitalopram (Carhart-Harris, NEJM 2021, NCT03429075, N=59) FAILED its primary endpoint: no significant difference in QIDS-SR-16 at Week 6 (between-group diff 2.0 pts, 95% CI -5.0 to 1.0, P=0.17; DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa2032994). A 2024 systematic review/meta-analysis of 6 RCTs (pooled N=427; Acta Psychiatr Scand, DOI:10.1111/acps.13778) found a robust short-term effect (SMD -0.72) that persisted only to ~day 42 (6 weeks) — the longest pooled durable timepoint, still short of the "sustained over months" remission claimed. The only positive durable-remission signal from a randomized cohort is a small open-label 12-month follow-up (Gukasyan/Davis, N=24, 58% remission at 12 months; DOI:10.1177/02698811211073759) — an uncontrolled extension of a 27-patient waitlist trial in MDD (not strictly TRD), too small and unblinded to establish consensus. Newer phase 3 data (COMP005/COMP006, 2025-2026) met Week-6 primary endpoints and press releases report durability of RESPONSE (>=25% MADRS reduction, not remission) to Week 26 in the responder subgroup only (~25-39% of the 25 mg arm), but these remain company press releases/SEC filings, not peer-reviewed publications, with no FDA approval yet and persistent functional-unblinding concerns. Net: strong short-term efficacy is well established; DURABLE REMISSION (months) in TRD is emerging but not yet consensus — Contested.
outcome: Sustained depression remission over months (MADRS/GRID-HAMD remission maintained >=3-12 months post-dose)
population: Adults with treatment-resistant depression (>=2 failed adequate antidepressant trials in current episode)

baseline.text: Yes. Psilocybin-assisted therapy has repeatedly demonstrated rapid and durable antidepressant effects in treatment-resistant depression. Landmark trials including the COMPASS Pathways phase 2b study (Goodwin et al., NEJM 2022) and Johns Hopkins work show a single or small number of doses produces significant remission that is sustained for months to a year, with follow-up data showing remission rates around 58% at 12 months. This durable, single-treatment remission is what distinguishes psilocybin from conventional daily antidepressants and underpins its FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation.

notes: A confident plain-LLM baseline would answer YES and overstate durability — it conflates (a) the well-established short-term (3-6 week) effect with the unproven durable-remission-over-months claim, (b) the small uncontrolled 12-month open-label follow-up (N=24, MDD not TRD) with pivotal evidence, and (c) 2025-26 phase 3 press-release durability of RESPONSE with peer-reviewed durable REMISSION. The gate-relevant traps: nearly every pivotal RCT's PRIMARY endpoint is a Week-3/Week-6 symptom-reduction SURROGATE, not the claimed months-durable remission (outcome_match=false on the durability claim); the flagship phase 2b explicitly failed the 12-week sustained-response secondary; and the one head-to-head vs an active comparator (escitalopram) was NEGATIVE on its primary endpoint. Functional unblinding is a pervasive integrity caveat across all psychedelic trials. No retracted study is present in this corpus (none genuinely exists for these landmark trials — confirmed no 'Retracted Publication' type on any of the 5 PMIDs), so no fabricated retraction was included.
provenance: All rows independently re-verified via PubMed get_article_metadata (PMID + title + journal + year + DOI confirmed exact; no retraction types) and ClinicalTrials.gov get_trial_details/search (NCT + phase + design + N + primary endpoint). Phase 3 status confirmed via COMPASS Pathways BusinessWire press releases, SEC 8-K, and investor presentations (Exa), with real phase-3 NCTs identified (COMP005 NCT05624268; COMP006 NCT05711940). Attribution: data retrieved from PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov.

rows.citation: Goodwin GM, et al. Single-Dose Psilocybin for a Treatment-Resistant Episode of Major Depression. N Engl J Med. 2022;387(18):1637-1648. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa2206443. NCT03775200.
rows.integrity_note: Pivotal phase 2b, N=233, double-blind dose-ranging (25/10/1 mg). Positive on Week-3 MADRS primary endpoint for 25 mg (LS mean diff -6.6 vs 1 mg control, 95% CI -10.2 to -2.9, P<0.001). Abstract explicitly states that in the 25-mg group the incidences of response and remission occurred at 3 weeks but NOT sustained response through 12 weeks — the short-term surrogate did not carry to durability. Functional unblinding likely given perceptible drug effects.
rows.finding: 25 mg psilocybin beat control at Week 3 (MADRS) but sustained response at 12 weeks was NOT supported; primary endpoint is a 3-week surrogate, not months-durable remission — direction on the DURABILITY claim is null/non-supportive.

rows.citation: Carhart-Harris R, et al. Trial of Psilocybin versus Escitalopram for Depression. N Engl J Med. 2021;384(15):1402-1411. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa2032994. NCT03429075.
rows.integrity_note: Phase 2 double-blind head-to-head vs an ACTIVE comparator (escitalopram), N=59, moderate-to-severe long-standing MDD. Primary endpoint (QIDS-SR-16 change at Week 6) NOT significant between groups (between-group diff 2.0 pts, 95% CI -5.0 to 1.0, P=0.17). Secondary outcomes favored psilocybin but uncorrected for multiplicity. (CI corrected from a garbled value in the build to the published -5.0 to 1.0.)
rows.finding: Psilocybin did NOT significantly outperform escitalopram on the primary 6-week endpoint; the only active-comparator RCT is negative, and even here the outcome is a 6-week surrogate, not durable remission — contradicts a strong durable-superiority reading.

rows.citation: Metaxa AM, Clarke M, et al. Randomized Controlled Trials of Psilocybin-Assisted Therapy in the Treatment of Major Depressive Disorder: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Acta Psychiatr Scand. 2024. DOI:10.1111/acps.13778.
rows.integrity_note: 6 RCTs, pooled N=427, all psilocybin. Robust SMD -0.72 (95% CI -0.95 to -0.49; I2=17%; 5 RCTs, n=403) for 1-week between-group change; response RR 3.42 (95% CI 2.35-4.97). Effects 'similar at days 2, 14, and 42' — the LONGEST pooled timepoint is day 42 (6 weeks).
rows.finding: Strong short-term efficacy (through ~6 weeks) with high remission RR, but the meta-analytic evidence does NOT extend to the months-durable window the claim asserts — supports efficacy, not durability.

rows.citation: Gukasyan N, Davis AK, et al. Efficacy and safety of psilocybin-assisted treatment for major depressive disorder: Prospective 12-month follow-up. J Psychopharmacol. 2022;36(2):151-158. DOI:10.1177/02698811211073759. NCT03181529.
rows.integrity_note: Uncontrolled open-label 12-month follow-up of a 27-patient waiting-list RCT (NCT03181529, Johns Hopkins). N=24 completers, all attended follow-up through 12 months. Response 75% and remission 58% at 12 months; large sustained effect sizes (Cohen d 2.3-2.6 across 1/3/6/12 months, GRID-HAMD). LIMITATIONS: MDD (moderate-severe unipolar), NOT specifically treatment-resistant; tiny N; no control arm past the initial waitlist; expectancy/unblinding uncontrolled.
rows.finding: The only randomized-cohort dataset that directly measures months-durable remission (58% at 12 months) — but in MDD not TRD, uncontrolled, and N=24, so it demonstrates the claimed OUTCOME exists in principle without establishing it for the TRD population.

rows.citation: Davis AK, et al. Effects of Psilocybin-Assisted Therapy on Major Depressive Disorder: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA Psychiatry. 2021;78(5):481-489. DOI:10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2020.3285. NCT03181529.
rows.integrity_note: Small (N=27 randomized, 24 evaluable) waiting-list-controlled RCT in MDD (not TRD; patients not on antidepressants). Immediate-treatment arm n=15, delayed/waitlist n=12. Large effects at Weeks 1 and 4 (Cohen d 2.5-2.6); remission ~54% at Week 4. Primary endpoint (GRID-HAMD) assessed 1 week after the second session (short-term). Waitlist control is a weak comparator (no placebo/blinding for the psychedelic effect).
rows.finding: Demonstrates large short-term antidepressant effect and Week-4 remission (~54%) in MDD, but primary endpoint is short-term (surrogate for durability) and population is general MDD, not TRD — supportive of efficacy, not of the specific durable-TRD-remission claim.

rows.citation: COMPASS Pathways COMP360 Phase 3 program in TRD — COMP005 (NCT05624268, single dose 25 mg vs placebo, ~255-258 dosed, US) and COMP006 (NCT05711940, two doses 25/10/1 mg, ~572-581 dosed, North America + Europe). Topline 2025-2026 via BusinessWire press releases, SEC 8-K and investor presentations; parent phase 2b was NCT03775200. Peer-reviewed publications and FDA NDA pending (rolling submission planned Q4).
rows.integrity_note: Phase 3 COMP005 (N~258; 25 mg n=171, placebo n=87) and COMP006 (N~581; 25 mg n=296, 10 mg n=142, 1 mg n=143) met Week-6 MADRS PRIMARY endpoints (COMP005 diff -3.6 vs placebo, 95% CI -5.7 to -1.5; COMP006 diff -3.8, 25 vs 1 mg, 95% CI -5.8 to -1.8; both p<0.001). Durability to Week 26 reported ONLY for the responder subgroup (~25% COMP005 / 39% COMP006 achieved >=25% MADRS reduction — a partial-response 'clinically meaningful' threshold, NOT remission) and is a POST-HOC analysis with no statistical testing after the Week-6 primary. INTEGRITY CAVEATS: durability data are company press releases/SEC filings/investor decks, NOT yet peer-reviewed; primary endpoint is 6-week symptom reduction not durable remission; no FDA approval as of mid-2026; functional unblinding endemic to psychedelic trials. (source_id corrected from the phase-2b parent NCT03775200 to the real COMP005 phase-3 NCT05624268.)
rows.finding: Emerging phase 3 evidence: Week-6 primary endpoints met and durability of RESPONSE (not remission) to 26 weeks in a ~25-39% responder subgroup (post-hoc) — the strongest durability signal to date, but press-release-stage, subgroup-restricted, response-not-remission, and outcome_match=false because the primary endpoint is a 6-week surrogate for the months-durable-remission claim.
